143.title: Differentials — poor feeding neonate
143.subtitle: Near-miss diagnoses to process before you close the case.

items.label: Duodenal obstruction / malrotation
items.why: Vomiting after feeds — but classically **bilious** emesis and surgical abdomen. Timing overlaps, yet you will not see elevated galactose or deficient **GALT** on RBCs.
items.discriminator: Obstruction = mechanical blockage after feeds. Galactosemia = **milk sugar toxin** → jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataracts, sepsis risk.

items.label: E. coli sepsis (galactosemic infants)
items.why: Galactosemic neonates are at **increased sepsis risk** — fever, tachycardia, lethargy overlap. Blood cultures may still be sent, but the **newborn screen / galactose level** and **GALT assay** anchor the metabolic diagnosis.
items.discriminator: Treat infection if present — but do not miss stopping **galactose** while you work up sepsis.

items.label: Biliary atresia / obstructive cholestasis
items.why: Conjugated hyperbilirubin and acholic stools — persistent jaundice beyond the first weeks. This infant's crisis tracks **milk feeds** and metabolic toxin, not isolated bile duct obliteration.
items.discriminator: Feed-locked symptoms + elevated galactose → metabolic, not primary surgical biliary disease.

items.label: Hypoglycemia from blocked gluconeogenesis
items.why: Not a separate diagnosis — it is a **consequence** of GALT blockade. Hepatocytes cannot route galactose into glycolysis → **ATP crash** → lethargy, poor feeding, seizures.
items.discriminator: Check glucose, but the fix is still **eliminate galactose** and confirm **GALT** deficiency.
